faqs.q: Should you add gable vents or a power fan to a Montclair roof that already has a ridge vent?

runs.v: No. Two exhaust types over one attic short-circuit the airflow, per the Roof Assembly Ventilation Coalition, and a power fan paired with a ridge vent pulls outdoor air down through the ridge instead of up from the soffits.

faqs.q: How much attic ventilation does a Montclair home need?

runs.v: At least 1/150 of the attic floor in net free vent area under IRC Section R806.2, split roughly 50% soffit intake and 50% ridge exhaust; on a multi-gabled Victorian or Tudor roof, each attic compartment is sized on its own.

faqs.q: Should you choose a passive ridge vent or a powered attic fan in Montclair?

runs.v: A passive ridge-and-soffit system ranks ahead of a powered attic fan, because a powered or solar fan depressurizes the attic and draws conditioned air from the living space, per the U.S. DOE Building America Solution Center and Building Science Corporation (Joseph Lstiburek).

faqs.q: How do I replace a roof vent?

runs.v: A roofer lifts the shingles above the old vent, pulls its nails, checks the deck for rot, slides the new vent's upper flange under the shingles above it, fastens it, and seals the exposed fasteners. Replacement is necessary when a vent is cracked or its seal has failed; if the deck around the opening is soft, the repair grows into a deck repair.
